title: Network & DNS
summary: Name lookups, address conflicts, domain trust, time sync and secure connections.

events.title: A name lookup timed out
events.meaning: Windows asked a DNS server to look up a name and got no answer in time. The message names it.
events.causes: A slow or unreachable DNS server, a network problem, or a wrong DNS setting.
events.next: Check the DNS servers set for the network adapter and that you can reach them.

events.title: Another device is using this PC's IP address
events.meaning: Windows found that another device on the network has the same IP address.
events.causes: Two devices set to the same fixed address, or a DHCP problem.
events.next: Give one of the devices a different address, or use automatic addressing.

events.title: No domain controller could be reached
events.meaning: This PC could not find a domain controller to sign in with.
events.causes: A network or DNS problem, a VPN that is not connected, or the controller is down.
events.next: Check the network, DNS and VPN, and that the domain controller is reachable.

events.title: This PC could not authenticate with a domain controller
events.meaning: The PC's trust with the domain failed, so it may deny sign-ins.
events.causes: The PC's computer account password is out of date, or the account was removed.
events.next: Check the domain connection. You may need to rejoin the PC to the domain.

events.title: The clock has not synced for a long time
events.meaning: The Windows Time service has not been able to sync the clock for a while.
events.causes: The time source is unreachable, blocked, or set wrongly.
events.next: Check the time source setting and that it can be reached.

events.title: The time service could not find a time source
events.meaning: The Windows Time service could not set up a source to sync the clock with.
events.causes: A DNS problem or an unreachable time server.
events.next: Check DNS and the configured time server.

events.title: A secure connection failed: no shared encryption
events.meaning: A device tried to connect securely, but no encryption setting was supported by both sides.
events.causes: An old program or device using outdated TLS settings.
events.next: Update the program or device, or check the TLS settings on both sides.

events.title: A secure connection received an error alert
events.meaning: The other side of a secure connection sent a fatal alert and the connection was closed.
events.causes: A certificate problem, a mismatch in settings or a broken connection.
events.next: Check the alert code in the message and the certificate on the other side.
